 South Dakota Ranks No. 2 for Student Loan Repayment Affordability
 South Dakota ranks second nationally for student loan repayment affordability. About 110,600 borrowers held $3.4 billion in federal student loan debt, with an estimated average monthly payment of $341.
 By Dominic Archer November 20, 2026 8:00 am

 MITCHELL, SD ( Mitchell Now ) — South Dakota ranks second in the nation for student loan repayment affordability, finishing 0.31 points behind North Dakota in Student Choice’s 50-state index. South Dakota scored 58.15, with lower scores indicating greater affordability. 
 How much do South Dakota borrowers owe?
 About 110,600 South Dakota borrowers held $3.4 billion in federal student loan debt. The average balance was $30,741, the second lowest in the country. The estimated monthly payment was also second lowest at $341, or $78 below the national estimate of $419. Student Choice assumed a 5.99% interest rate and a standard 10-year repayment term.
 The estimated payment equaled 5.2% of South Dakota’s per capita personal income of $78,999. In the fourth quarter of 2025, 5.8% of the state’s outstanding student loan balances were at least 90 days past due, compared with 7.3% in North Dakota and nearly 10% nationwide. 
 What factors went into the ranking?
 Student Choice weighted estimated payments relative to income at 40%, delinquency at 20%, rent relative to income and household debt relative to income at 15% each, and cost of living at 10%. South Dakota’s median gross rent was 26.9% of household income, and its cost-of-living index was 93.5, below the national benchmark of 100. 
 Wisconsin, New Hampshire and Massachusetts rounded out the top five. Mississippi ranked last, with estimated payments equal to 9.2% of per capita income and 13.4% of outstanding student loan balances at least 90 days past due.
